subject: Procurement path check — PO vs card and marketplace billing for trial conversion
messages:
From: Karhtik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Renee Caldwell <rcaldwell@brightops.com>, Peter Zhao <pzhao@brightops.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & ask: procurement path options (PO vs card), marketplace interest, trial-to-paid triggers

Thanks for the time today — quick written recap and clear next steps so procurement has something to act on. Great call, Peter and Renee.

Summary (from our discovery):
- Technical: BrightOps will run a 30-day pilot for the agent orchestration use case (~15-20 agents, expected ~500k tokens/week).
- Success criteria: 1) Stable agent integrations (2 critical flows), 2) >=10 active agents on platform, OR >=1,000,000 tokens consumed during pilot. These align to your internal KPIs for the PoC.
- Procurement: you indicated procurement typically uses a PO workflow (Ariba). You also asked about the possibility of using AWS Marketplace billing or a corporate card for initial payment.

Questions we need to confirm from procurement:
1) Preferred commercial path: PO via Ariba (invoiced by Redwood) OR credit card / Marketplace purchase.
2) AP billing contact + invoice delivery address (email + postal for PO).
3) Any legal terms required up front (MSA vs SOW) and whether DocuSign is acceptable.
4) Approximate expected monthly spend if pilot converts (ballpark $/month) so we can generate the right quote.

Suggested commercial options from our side:
- Option A: Direct PO (Ariba) -> Redwood sends invoice monthly after billing start.
- Option B: AWS Marketplace listing -> BrightOps buys via Marketplace (may simplify procurement but depends on your Marketplace procurement policies).
- Option C: Card for initial 30-day pilot, then PO if you convert.

Billing start recommendation: we typically allow customers to pick either a calendar date (e.g., first of the month after pilot) or a usage-trigger (billing begins when success criteria met or when cumulative tokens exceed X). For your use case I recommend: billing starts when either the 1M token threshold is hit OR on the scheduled pilot end date (whichever comes first). If procurement requires a PO to be issued before any charges, we’ll align to that flow.

Next steps (proposed):
- Renee/Peter: confirm procurement route (PO via Ariba vs card vs marketplace) and AP contact for invoice delivery.
- Karhtik: will send a formal quote + MSA (DocuSign) and a compliance package (SOC2 link).
- Marissa: will share SOC2 and support for security questionnaire.

Attachments sent after the thread: Redwood-quote-BrightOps-20260324.pdf (quote), MSA-Redwood-BrightOps-2026.docx (MSA draft).

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the quote in the next hour so procurement can attach it to the PO request.

— Karhtik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karhtik.iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Renee Caldwell <rcaldwell@brightops.com>
To: Karhtik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Peter Zhao <pzhao@brightops.com>
Cc: Mark Peterson <ap@brightops.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & ask: procurement path options (PO vs card), marketplace interest, trial-to-paid triggers

Thanks Karhtik — helpful recap. A couple quick answers from procurement here: 

- Procurement process: BrightOps prefers PO via Ariba for any vendor engagement above $5k/month. We will need a vendor quote and the supplier details to create a PR/PO.
- Invoice requirements: invoices should be sent to ap@brightops.com; please include our PO number when issued and W-9 if required.
- Marketplace: AWS Marketplace is possible but would require us to go through our cloud procurement team and may add ~2 weeks to the paperwork. If there’s an equivalent PO flow through Marketplace, that would be ideal — otherwise direct PO is faster for us.
- Billing start: Procurement prefers billing start tied to the PO effective date. That said, if Redwood can delay invoicing until we confirm acceptance (post-pilot) and attach the PO retroactively, that would work as a pragmatic approach. Can you confirm Redwood’s flexibility on invoice timing?

Can you send the quote and redlined MSA draft to ap@brightops.com and me? I’ll pull in our legal if any term changes are proposed.

Thanks,
Renee
Head of IT Operations | BrightOps
rcaldwell@brightops.com | +1 (206) 555-8801
From: Karhtik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Renee Caldwell <rcaldwell@brightops.com>, Peter Zhao <pzhao@brightops.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Mark Peterson <ap@brightops.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 11:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & ask: procurement path options (PO vs card), marketplace interest, trial-to-paid triggers

Renee — appreciate the clarity. We can support the PO/Ariba flow. A few specifics and what I’m sending now: 

What I’m attaching (sent with this thread):
- Redwood-quote-BrightOps-20260324.pdf — line-item quote with SKU-level pricing and monthly estimate.
- MSA-Redwood-BrightOps-2026.docx — draft MSA (DocuSign link included below).
- W-9 and vendor remit details included in the quote PDF.

Invoice timing options we can support: 
1) Invoice effective date = PO effective date (preferred by procurement) — we can invoice from that date and accept PO as the trigger.
2) Retroactive invoicing: Redwood can accept a PO after pilot completion and invoice retroactively to the PO effective date for the pilot period (if procurement needs time to issue PO).
3) Usage-triggered billing: if you prefer, we can automatically start billing when the agreed success criteria are met (e.g., 1M tokens or 10 active agents).

Please confirm which option procurement prefers and who at AP should receive the quote. If AP wants a formal vendor setup form, we can fill it.

DocuSign MSA (draft): https://docusign.com/Redwood-MSA-BrightOps-2026
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/BRIGHT-2026-003

Marissa — looping you in to share SOC2 and to offer support for any security questionnaire. Laura — looping you to give pricing acceptance and MSA instruction for finance.

Best,
— Karhtik
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Renee Caldwell <rcaldwell@brightops.com>, Karhtik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & ask: procurement path options (PO vs card), marketplace interest, trial-to-paid triggers

Hi Renee — happy to help on the security/compliance side. Quick notes and attachments: 

- SOC2: attaching our SOC2 report (SOC2_report_2025.pdf) and a short compliance pack that explains data handling, retention, and support for vendor questionnaires. Link: https://s3.redwood.ai/compliance/SOC2_report_2025.pdf
- Data residency: Redwood’s hosted offering can route inference requests to us-east-1 or eu-west-1. If you need a private deployment we can scope that separately.
- Marketplace: confirming what Karhtik said — AWS Marketplace listing is supported but procurement needs to confirm whether Marketplace purchase can be accepted in lieu of an internal PO. Marketplace purchases sometimes require a different internal approval flow. If you want, I can loop in our marketplaces lead to coordinate the listing timeline and any procurement forms.

Trial-to-paid conversion checklist I recommend we agree on now (to avoid back-and-forth at the end):
1) Acceptance criteria: 2 critical flows integrated and smoke tests passing.
2) Usage threshold: 1,000,000 tokens OR 10 active agents for 3 consecutive days.
3) Billing trigger: PO effective date OR the date threshold is met (procurement to confirm).
4) Renewal: unless otherwise noted, we’ll convert to monthly billing with the quoted SKU pricing.

If procurement sends the PO (Ariba) to ap@brightops.com we’ll have finance intake it and confirm vendor setup within 2 business days.

Attaching: SOC2_report_2025.pdf (attachment stub)

— Marissa

Thanks everyone — getting aligned internally. Quick answers from our side: 

- We will proceed with PO via Ariba (faster for our legal/finance). AP contact is ap@brightops.com and Mark Peterson will submit the PO once he has the vendor quote and our internal approval.
- Expected spend if we convert: ~ $15k / month (ballpark). Please reflect this band in the quote so Mark can attach it to the PR.
- Billing start: Mark will try to issue the PO effective on the planned pilot start date; if we miss that the PO can be backdated to cover the pilot period. We prefer Redwood to invoice to the PO effective date once the PO is processed.

Action items: 
- Karhtik: please send the final quote and vendor remit ASAP to ap@brightops.com (Mark) and cc Renee. Mark needs the vendor name, remit address, and W-9 to process.
- Marissa: we will review the SOC2 and reach out if any gaps.

I’ll keep you posted once procurement issues the PR/PO. Looking forward to kicking off.

— Peter
